title: Preserve explicit command admission and independent interface contracts
statement: The system shall admit only explicitly selected supported command operations and inputs under their declared interface contracts, preserve independent version and outcome domains, and reject unsupported or ambiguous input at the required boundary without inventing selectors or operational support.

what.problem: Callers can accidentally invoke withdrawn commands, mix transport versions with stored versions, or supply ambiguous selectors that would direct unintended work.
what.desired_outcome: Each invocation has one understood public operation, exact input contract, and accurate response domain before dependent work begins.

why.rationale: Predictable admission prevents an automation client from acting on an unintended operation or fabricated contract selection.

stakeholders: Engineers and reviewers operating on recorded engineering work
Engineering agents acting on explicit actor decisions
Maintainers and consumers of the published command-line interface

conditions: For public command selection, help/version, current operational tasks, maintenance, installation and diagnostics.

contexts: Published command surfaces and their separately owned request, result, stored-record, document, configuration, and diagnostic version domains.

how.approach: Apply each command family’s closed grammar and required selectors before dependent access. Preserve independent request, response, stored-schema and backup versions; reject retired public interfaces without residue-based fallback.

how_much.scope: All current public command families and the exact declared retired set. Generic installation outcomes remain governed by Installation. This does not reintroduce compact, lifecycle, new-change, the withdrawn query shim, the spec configuration kind, or a REM-record CLI. The local operational-history extension adds the criteria attributed to SRC-LOCAL-OPERATIONAL-ANALYSIS; retained product contracts and old allocation evidence do not establish implementation or coverage of that extension.

acceptance_criteria: Recognized commands disclose operation-specific help without repository access when the contract requires it; help/version accurately identify supported commands and the delivered package.

Unknown or duplicate flags, extra positionals, missing or contradictory selectors, unsupported operations, and unknown configuration kinds reject before filesystem or stdin access where the owning command requires that order; rejected raw values are not echoed.

Operational v2 requests and schema-4 results, store-maintenance-v1 requests, installation schema-2 results and diagnostic interfaces retain independent version domains. No untrusted request or stored version selects another response family.

Retired or unknown ordinary record contracts, unsupported database schemas and mismatched projects receive safe rejection without conversion or fallback. Only explicit qualified maintenance may import selected supported source facts while preserving required originals.
Human and structured forms preserve each family’s defined actual outcome and exit meaning; presentation never establishes semantic approval.

Backup, restoration, transfer, migration and history queries require explicit supported project and scope selection. Storage schema versions, backup versions and command-interface versions are not interchangeable; wrong-project inputs reject before mutation.
